review_title: Impressed, a great upgrade from y Flex.
review_text:
After using a FitBit Flex for over a year, I decided to upgrade to one of the newer units.

The Charge is only a little larger than the Flex. Due to the electronics in the Charge, it is a one piece unit, unlike the Flex where you could change out the wristband.

With the Flex, I could use the Large band at either the last or next to last openings, the XL band was a bit more comfortable. With the Charge, I must wear it on the last opening. The XL version of the Charge is only available directly from FitBit, which means no discounts. As a one piece device, make sure you check your wrist size and compare against the FitBit sizing information.

I use the sleep tracking functionality of the Charge, it tracks your sleep automatically, unlike the Flex where you needed to put it into sleep mode or manually enter your sleep and awake times. I am very impressed with how accurate the Charge records my falling asleep and wake up times.

It also seems to be more accurate in regards to my active minutes. Step counts appear to be on par with the Flex. I like that it tracks floors climbed as my job requires that I go up and down a lot of steps each night (not a full floor at a time, typically 4-5 steps at a time).

It may seem like a silly thing, but the ability to see the name of the person calling your cellphone on the Charge has been very helpful (provided you have that person in your contacts, otherwise it only shows the telephone number). My job is fairly active, so my phone is generally in my pocket. This helps to see if I need to dig my phone out or let it go to voicemail.

I am quite happy with my purchase - other than I really wanted to get the Charge HR, which hasn't yet been released.

---
On another note, I had the original FitBit years ago, you can see my unflattering review of the product and the company at that time. I must say their support has improved 100%. The only reason I had the Flex was that it was given to me by a partner company of theirs. Otherwise I would not have even considered another FitBit product.

I got mine maybe a month before the Charge HR came out and I desperately want to get that one as well. This one tracks how many calories you burn but it's more of an estimation based on how many steps you take and the frequency of them. If you're looking for an even more accurate calories burned record, go for the Charge HR because it will use your heart rate to more accurately account for calories burned. Additionally, being able to see the progress I'm making towards my goals each day, throughout the day, is really motivating. The colors of the visual progress monitoring change as you get closer to your goal (both online and on the iPhone app) and it's really motivating! Don't question whether or not to get one, just get it! I've gotten them as gifts to many family members and they all love it too.

review_text:
I bought this Fitbit Charge because I lost my Fitbit One--twice, even while wearing it correctly with the clip and everything. So, I decided to try out a wristband version that I hopefully won't lose!!
First, Customer Service at FitBit is excellent. Both times that I lost anything--first when the clip broke, and then when the fitbit entirely fell off my bra--they replaced the broken or missing parts immediately. Only once my warranty expired and I lost my One again did I decide to try the wristband.
So far, I am loving my Charge! It counts things relatively accurately (on a stairmaster, it did not record stairs taken, but that could be because of the way I hold the machine rather than actually swing my arms). I love the display and the texture of the wristband.
The only reason I don't give it a 5 star rating is the bulkiness of it. It doesn't bend with my wrist, and is slightly wider than my wrist so it kind of sticks out and gets stuck under my sleeves. I kind of feel like I'm wearing a bulky parole watch or something. The One was much more comfortable, and I kind of miss my little One.
Overall, though, I do love FitBit as a company and I love all their products!!

review_title: Flawed Design for People Who Sweat
review_text:
First one lasted nearly 6 months. Fitbit sent me a replacement. It lasted 6 days. Fitbit sent me another replacement. It lasted 3 days. I've given up. The contacts for recharging are exposed and if you sweat much, it shorts them out and the battery instantly discharges, which means it can't keep track of your steps until you recharge it. Since the unit does not take a standard USB cable to discharge it, you can simply recharge it anywhere unless you carry the special cable with you.
Also, the unit is not waterproof at all, so sweat creeps in the recharging opening and ruins the display. It is an absolutely terrible design for a product that is to be used to encourage exercise--if you sweat, it ruins it. Recharging is a hassle because it does not take a standard USB cable and you have to recharge about every six days, if the unit does not randomly discharge. I had a Garmin before this and it was at least 10 times better.
I will say that Fitbit customer service has been excellent and they have promptly sent me replacements. Unfortunately, their product is terrible. I won't be buying anymore Fitbit products for a long time.

review_title: Stylish, Accurate, But Needs Some Tweaking
review_text:
Many years ago I began with a Garmin Forerunner, but then moved to the Vivoactive, and then the Vivoactive HR. The Vivoactive 3 Music watch seemed like the natural progression.

Style: I love the Rosegold color. Watch looks and feels great. It comes with several stock watch faces, with plenty more from Garmin Connect. Most watch faces can be customized to a degree. The watch face that I liked the most, however, did not permit a battery indicator on the main screen, so I had to switch to my next favorite. Some details on the watch face are hard to pick out with my reader glasses, but a younger person won't have that trouble.

Battery: Herein lies the biggest disappointment. My old Vivoactive HR (when new) would go almost two weeks before needing a recharge, even with tracking activities. The Vivoactive 3 Music is only lasting about 3 days. Obviously, one can improve the battery life by turning off the notifications and heart rate monitor, and not using the music player during workouts. However, it's for those things that I bought the watch. So, I purchased an extra charger and keep one in my car and one at my desk to keep it ready to go.

Heart Rate: I've tested the HR monitor against a chest strap and found it to be accurate. The built-in widget provides the last 4 hours of HR monitoring, but the web based app on my computer allows me to check out the entire day as well as my history. Very nice.

GPS tracking: I run, bike, and walk. These respective apps allow me to easily check distance, time, and pace with a quick glance or swipe. Very satisfied.

Step counter: Although I've never personally tested the step counter, I've read other tests that suggest Garmin is not leading the pack when it comes to step counting accuracy. In any event, it's okay with me. Close is good enough for me.

Stress Monitor: This widget is new for me as it did not appear on the Vivoactive HR. It is designed to measure the stress you are experiencing throughout the day. It also has a feature that directs you through a stress reduction/measurement exercise. This is done though breathing in and out and holding your breath on cues. Seems cool, but so far I'm not finding it terribly useful.

Music: One of the main reasons I went with the Vivoactive 3 Music is because of the ability to play music while on a run without taking my phone. Two things that were a little disappointing: 1) it will not play WMA files (much of my music library), and 2) as a Google Play subscriber I cannot sync my Google Play song lists on the watch. After converting my music to MP3s, I was able to download and play. This worked perfectly. No skipping in my Bluetooth headphones, and no connectivity problems. I'm satisfied, but would be very happy to see a Google Play app added.

Garmin Wallet: The 3 Music allows you to preload a credit card number in its "wallet." You can then swipe the watch near a scanner in a store to use as a credit card. I've used it once and it worked flawlessly. Cool.

Sleep tracking: I really got hooked on the sleep tracking feature of my Vivoactive and Vivoactive HR watches. It really helped me understand why I was dragging on some days even though I felt like I had a good night. Therefore, I was excited to hear that the 3 Music contained sleep enhanced tracking.

The 3 Music does have enhanced tracking. However, it is still confusing to me. I was used to getting 3-4 hours of "deep sleep" every night. Now, I get under an hour of deep sleep because it is broken up into REM sleep. I still haven't figured out my "sweet spot" for sleep yet. I'm comparing how I feel throughout the day to my deep and REM sleep, but I haven't noticed a pattern yet. This has been a bit disappointing to me. Hopefully, I can figure it out.

I gave it four stars in stead of five because of the confusion over the sleep app and the inability to fully customize all watch faces. However, I really loves this watch and am looking forward to learning more about it.

review_text:
I bought this watch back in 2019 when I was looking into Garmin products. After 3 years of ownership, this watch can truly stand the test of time.

Pros:
- Durable; I have 1 hairline crack after 3 years and it's barely noticeable. I am pretty active and this watch endures a lot of punishment

- Accurate; the watch is great at measuring heart rate, stress, sleep, and VO2 max.

- Easy to use; With the App, this watch is easy to use and is very versatile. Great for runs, cycling, swimming, and general strength training.

-Programable; If you like to do specific workouts when it comes to cardio, don't worry, this watch has a lot of features that allow you to program a workout with ease!

Cons:
- Rubber band irritates skin; After constant wearing, the rubber band will cause rashing and itchiness on my skin. After about 2 years of use, the band broke. If you get this watch, upgrade it with a metal band. Much more comfortable and durable.

- Distance tracker can be inaccurate; If it is bad weather, the distance tracker may be off. I ran 2 miles on a tack and it said I only ran 1.94. This was on a very cloudy day and usually, it's only off by 0.01 or 0.02 regularly. However, you can manually adjust the total distance in the workout summary, so it's not a big problem if you ask me.

- Limited text responses; There are about 4 or 5 small replies you can use to send quick texts back to whoever is messaging you. Not a problem for me, but some may find this annoying.

- Limited display settings; The stock displays are alright, I just wish there were more. Maybe there is and I am ignorant.

Overall I love this watch and will probably use it until I break it or lose it. Regardless of the cons, this watch stands in cruel conditions and is accurate over 98% of the time. A must-buy if you are in the military or have an active lifestyle.

review_text: This was offered by a company called LifeQInc, and was $229, which was about $70 cheaper than most other offerings. The description said it was open box, but unused, and still had the screen protector. There's another offering on Amazon for $200 that is called certified refurbished, and I don't know how good it is, but this open box model was just as advertised. The box was not sealed, but it was packed just like an untouched, sealed version. There was no evidence that anyone had ever opened the box. The watch is perfect; I've really been excited about it. When I run it tracks my heart rate, my stress, my steps, by mileage, and my route, and the screen display is so clear and bright that I don't need to be wearing my glasses. It vibrates on every mile and lights up so I can see at a glance my pace. When I get back to my cell phone it instantly syncs and I can see detailed profiles of all my biometrics, plus a map of my route. The Garman Connect app on the computer has a very nice review, of daily steps, runs, sleep stages, stress....  I also got the free strava app, and it also syncs and has at least one more metric, and compares your times with other runners on the same route. If you're a serious racer, you'll want to pay for the strava app, but if you're just a casual runner you will probably find the Garman connect app perfect. It also allows you to load other apps for different purposes. I like that it reminds me to move every so often, because I tend to sit at my desk for hours.

review_title: Love it, great daily watch, fitness tracker and sports watch
review_text: I had been using another fitness teaching watch, but find I was wanting more than it was capable of as I started doing more training and different running workouts. I had waited a while to jump to Garmin because I never thought of myself as a true "runner", but as I started doing more the Garmin watches did everything I was wanting and more. I did a lot of research before deciding, but the price point for the vivoavtive 3 music was within reach, it allows me to run without my phone and still have music (hate the armbands!, most of my running pants have pockets now but still not ideal), and the size of the watch face is now smaller to better for my wrist while still being able to see all the tracking easily during my run. It's super comfortable to wear as a daily watch, you can change the watch face to suit what you like and what you want to do for daily tracking, and can easily scroll through your commonly used widgets, and has enough smartwatch capabilities like text and call notification, weather, calendar reminders, (plus you can download more apps if you want). Tracking exercises is super easy, GPS locks quickly and is accurate, and Garmin gives you tons of dynamics about your run or workout. Heart rate monitoring seems accurate (or as accurate as any other wrist based model), and gives you further info about your training and day. Garmin has some pre-set workouts,in or you can create your own and load them, which I really liked! I had no issues losing music into it, I use Google play music and just downloaded songs onto my computer then transferred them to the watch (more detailed directions on Garmin or various YouTube videos). I don't have one of the verified Bluetooth wireless headphones, or even one of the big brands, but had no trouble pairing them and so far so good... Will try on a longer run this weekend. It tracks your steps and you can turn on a "move reminder" if you've been inactive for too long, nice for at work as a gentle reminder to get up from my desk. The vibration alerts can be set to different vibration levels (low/med/high) which is nice. I haven't had any issues with battery life wearing it daily to work and doing a few runs with GPS and no music before needing to charge. Of course running with GPS and music will drain it more quickly, but it charges pretty fast. Even though the construction and materials seem solid and study, I did decide to purchase a screen protector because I'm a little rough on my watches, so better safe than sorry. Overall after just a week I'm really loving it and those I made the jump over to Garmin.

review_title: This is a fantastic watch for the active person.  A STEP Ahead of past technologies
review_text:
Let me start by saying, I love this watch and am thrilled with it. Works great, just as it should and is an indispensable part of my life now that I have it. Here are the details:

Set-Up:
-Download the Garmin Connect App
-Charge your watch
-Connect with Bluetooth on your phone (I use iPhone)

The App:
-Shows you a daily summary of what you are doing and when you click on that item there is further detail.
-It will show your activities of that day such as walking, running, swimming.
-Current Heart Rate and Resting and High
-Current number of steps, goal and how many miles that equates to
-Number of floors you have climbed and how it compares to your goal
-Stress (Which I am not sure how that is calculated)
-Calories Burned based upon a guess with your activity level
-Your sleep from the previous night.

A few things I really like from the App:
-Activity such as running shows lots of detail like obviously distance, but time and pace and calories and elevation gain or loss. It even shows the temperature it was a the time of the activity.
-Sleep shows total amount excluding any time you are awake. It shows Deep, Light, REM and then Awake time. There is a great graph.
-There is also a weekly summary of your sleep.

The Watch itself:
-You can download a number of different watch faces to vary the look and have more or less information available to you on the face.
-You can scroll through things via swiping up and down or via the side of the watch.
-There is a menu accessible through pressing a button on the side.
-I have found the ability to skip to the next song helpful as it is connected to my phone so if I am listening to a Bluetooth speaker and am in the shower or away from the speaker and phone I can still skip a song or it will show me what is playing.
-The steel gray color is great looking.
Summary: I generally don't swipe through the watch much but it does receive all of my text messages and shows me when a phone call comes in and who it is (If they are in my phone) and when I get a voicemessage. You cannot respond on your phone, but you can read entire text messages. Great to know you are not missing a call. Vibration is good.

What I didn't like as much:
-If you don't move for awhile, the watch will vibrate and say MOVE. I don't need it to tell me that. Also, it vibrates when you reach certain goals like floors or steps. I don't need that.
-The Strength Counter is OK but through the app its a bit awkward. It gets the rep counts right maybe 80% of the time and doesn't really get the exercises right but that's a bit much to ask. You need to then go back in and enter the weight if you want. What I do like about the strength is that you can do a set and then double tap and it will say the set is done and then you it will count the time for your rest which is really helpful.
-The accuracy of running on trails is generally very good, but on trails where there is a mile counter it was off by about 3%. Not horrible, but it would be nice to be a bit closer.

Overall, a great item for the person looking to track their runs and sleep, easy to use and great looking. Also, excellent battery life. If you use GPS mode a lot during a day I would say expect 30 hours. If not, I would expect 3 days or so. If you don't do anything you could get probably 6.

review_title: Great watch/fitness tracker with amazing battery life
review_text:
First off, I had a pebble time smartwatch. Which in my opinion was the one of the best smartwatches period. After pebble was purchased by Fitbit it was hard to find another smartwatch that came close to the battery life and had an always-on screen. This watch does all that.

Let me say, I get an easy 7-8 days off battery life out of this watch. That is with my personal settings, you will not get 7-8 days if use the stock settings of the watch. More like 5 days with stock settings.

The watch is extremely comfortable to wear and it's pretty much unnoticeable after a few days of wearing it.

Another upside is that the watch is not too thick. I also tried out the ticwatch pro but it was just too thick for my liking. Coming in at 11.7mm this is one of the thinner smartwatches out there.

The Garmin connect app is also very detailed and intuitive. And the Garmin IQ app and gives you thousands of watch faces to choose from.

So it's thin has great battery life and it has an always-on screen. What's not to like.

To achieve a 7-8 day battery life set the backlight to 0%. Then change the face on the watch to have a white background and black text for the numbers and info. Then the watch is pretty much readable in any lighting condition except complete dark. That will give you the best battery life. Checkout the photos to see what I mean about the watchface. The last photo was taken in a very dark room and you can clearly see how visible it is. Also not using GPS everyday helps too. I still get that 7-8 days battery life with about an 2 hours of GPS usage, responding to notifications and using the Garmin pay features. The blacklight turns on every time you interact with the watch, that's why turning it off by going to 0% is crucial for battery life in watch.

This watch is great, just get it. It's worth every penny.

I believe my old pedometers would randomly jump up tens of steps because of some random movement, or driving around in a bumpy old work truck all day. I haven't seen any suspicious step patterns occur yet with the Fitbit. My only complaint is that with the sleep mode, the regular did not seem to catch all the times I was awake, but Im pretty sure the sensitive mode is catching when I am dreaming (the patterns are regular) and then telling me I was restless all of those times. All in all, this is a decent product and I definitely suggest picking up a few of the Bitbelts for added piece of mind.

review_title: Flex helped me understand where I was going wrong
review_text:
I got a Fitbit Flex from Amazon at the end of July. In the five months I have worn the Flex, I have lost nine pounds. Many reviewers say that it is just a pedometer, but it is much more than that if used correctly.

The wrist placement is a huge advantage for me. I have had three simple pedometers which were placed in a pocket previously. Each pedometer died when I washed the pants, forgetting to remove the pedometer from the pocket first. I don't have to worry about doing this again with the Flex. I only have to charge the Flex about once a week.

I log all my meals with the Flex, and have it set so that I eat 500 calories per day less than I use up. I don't think the calorie count estimate is completely accurate, but it works well enough that I have lost nine pounds. Just logging meals helps me understand what I'm eating, and has a deterrent effect to overeating. I don't bother logging meals during times like right now, when my daughter is home from college. Before I had the Flex I would try to exercise the weight off, with no real success. This used to work for me when I was in my 20s and 30s, but I'm over 50 now. The Flex proved to me that I had to cut my caloric intake in order to lose weight.

Other things I have learned: 1) I feel better when I drink more water. I was a skeptic about the 8 glasses of water per day, and I still don't think that is a hard and fast rule. But I try to drink at least 6 glasses a day, and the Flex helps me meet that goal.
2) I get enough sleep but have frequent interruptions, many due to the cat. I also would sometimes think I was lying awake for hours, but the Flex showed me that during most such episodes I am actually dozing on and off, not staying consistently awake.

review_text:
I wanted to count my steps and I wanted simple. I knew that a wrist based product would work better with me (I would lose or wash/dry the waistband/clothing clip-on style). I have had the opportunity to test it against known step counts and distances and it has been remarkably accurate.

It is perhaps too simple. Unlike my wife's waistband fit-bit, this model has no LCD display of information. Rather, it has a cryptic set of 5 LED lights which can light up independently or simultaneously, in certain patterns, thereby imparting relevant information, which would be requested by a series of taps designed to communicate one's inquiry such as, "How many steps have I gone?" --this would be a double-tap inquiry. If you have achieved 20% of your daily goal, then the answer is one light is solid and the next light will blink at a pace which hastens as the next 20% marker is approached. Got it?

If I want to send my unit into sleep monitoring I tap it real fast for more than 2 seconds. Once this monitoring has started, the unit vibrates and blinks two LEDs slowly out. Or mow the grass with a push mower and it it enters the sleep monitoring mode. Anything that shakes your arm will trigger this on and off. However at night when I use it, it is very accurate at monitoring my restfulness.

If a short hand Morse-code and blinking light style communication with your pedometer sounds appealing, then the durability and performance will please you - but if you like easy - wait for the next iteration.

I still like this product, and owning it has goaded me into 60% more steps than I had been taking. The online component is excellent, but the APPs are not consistent. The Android APP from Fit-Bit which my wife uses is awesome, but my Microsoft 8 APP is disappointingly lacking in the features that I saw in the Android.

The charging is easy, but the dongle and the charger could have been combined. Why should I use up two USB slots on my computer for one device? My charges last 6 days easily and I use mine for 12500+ a day. It has never been below 20% -- guess what the charge level - also another informative blinking light display.

review_title: Great Product for the Available Tech
review_text:
I understand the frustrations of some of the reviewers - doesn't count EVERY step, water stays in the wristband, calories are a bit off, you can't sync 2 devices - but you paid $100. This isn't a $10,000 piece of hardware developed by DARPA and it far exceeds the accuracy and enjoyment (and sometimes style) of the other comparably priced bulky, ugly, and bland fitness bands out there. And the largest appeal, at least for me, is not how accurately it tracks every step I take or every calorie I burn, but how much it motivates me, through competition with myself or with friends on Fitbit.com, to get in better shape and be healthier. And step accuracy with little error tolerance has little to do with that.

The biggest flaws I've found have been the lack of an altimeter, the absence stationary alarm, and Android support. Since the prior was in the Fitbit One (and is a hardware option that can't be fixed by firmware updates), it seems like a questionable decision to leave it out. But there might have been reasons (cost, size, demand, etc.) for that. The second issue is the stationary alarm. I've heard time and again that people would like to have the Flex vibrate when they have been inactive for a specified period of time. This is an easy implementation and I hope Fitbit adds it with a firmware update. Lastly, for Android devices, Fitbit will only currently sync with the Note 2 and Galaxy SIII. This needs to be expanded, and I'm sure it will be in the coming months.

The community appeal, while there, can be better. Adding friends is simple enough, but Fitbit.com and its App could benefit from adding additional badges, adding competitions and incentives, and really building their community. Anyone can make the hardware - it's the software, community support, and competition that make Fitbit desirable.

I've run tests with my Fitbit One and Flex on at the same time and all of the numbers (with the exception of stairs climbed, due to aforementioned reasons) seem to be close. The Fitbit One seems to be a bit more generous (it's hard to say if it's more accurate; the One just records more steps than my Flex), but it's not a big issue for me. So if I'm really that concerned about tracking my steps to within a 1% tolerance, I would probably need to invest in some better (and far more expensive) tech.

So if the benefit of having the Fitbit Flex as a wristband outweighs the numbers being slightly off those of the Fitbit One and the lack of the altimeter, and you can wait at least another month (some sites list ship dates as far as 10 weeks out), I say go for it. Else, go with the Fitbit One, another exceptional product.

review_text:
I really like this watch...but I like the app best of all!!

The watch is comfortable to wear and the controls are easy to use. The accuracy of outdoor running distances is very good. The heart rate monitor seems fairly accurate compared to manual measurement in most cases. The one feature that does not seem to work well is the indoor run distance tracker; it is way off compared to my treadmill but frankly this feature isn’t really that important to me and the watch could probably do without it.

When you pair the watch to a phone you are alerted when your phone rings or you get a text. You can see who is calling or read the text without looking at your phone. The app gives a lot of cool information for each run (distance, split times, split paces, average pace, elevation gain, heart rate, cadence, route, steps, and many more). It also tracks total daily steps, 24/7 heart rate, and estimates VO2 max, among others. The real-time pace lags a bit so it would be difficult to do accurate interval-type workouts. I don’t cycle or swim so I can’t speak to those features.

The sleep tracking app is pretty cool, but I can’t verify the accuracy of light and deep sleep totals because...who knows? I do know that the app does make me more conscious of when I go to bed and how much sleep I get.

My wish for this watch would be a bigger button for starting and stopping the timer (years ago I had an old pre-GPS Nike watch and its start/stop button was nice and large and easy to locate and press while running). Any watch I have had since has made me wonder why the button isn’t more pronounced, but I think most everything on the market has a small button. But I digress...

Overall this watch is a very good buy for its price point, especially when you use the app/pair to a phone. There are many cool features and lots of data in the app that definitely make you more mindful of your health and activity. I would definitely recommend!

review_title: Great for almost any kind of cardio training. Wish it had a couple extra features.
review_text:
For running, jogging, hiking, biking or just walking this is one of the better trackers money can buy.
I've tried 3 now, Samsung, MioFuse and this one.
The garmin is by far the better choice for typical Cardio fitness.
The heart rate monitor does a pretty good job, a few times when i checked it it seemed to be paused or something at like 80bpms and then suddenly jumped to 130 a second after I checked it.
I've worn it in the pool, the shower and the hot tub, still works perfectly. Also the glass seems to be relatively scratch resistant, that or I've just gotten lucky (I'm not nice to these things).
It does a great job of saving your routines and even automatically saves them in-case you forget.
Set up is pretty simple but syncing to the phone requires a download of garmins program and an account set-up. Was a bit of a PITA.
For Interval training like HIIT it also works well but is a more tedious to set up.
And for timed training that needs to be variable, forget it, there's no real timer and you can use the interval function but it gets even more difficult if you need to adjust times on the fly.
Honestly those are my only few gripes. I do a lot of weight training and need to be able to time my rest periods, I just wont use the Garmin for that. I would love a device that lets me time my sets and then start a pre-set rest period, then records all of it.
The Interval function almost does this and I've learned how to manipulate it to get what I want but it's not as intuitive as I'd like.
Still this is a nit picky way to use it for a specialized routine.
But when I get on the cardio machines or hit the trail for a hike it's a great companion.
It syncs well with my fitness pal as well.

Overall its loaded with functions, easy to read and use for standard cardio training, does a great job synching and saving routines, durable, comfortable. I really cant complain. It's definitely better than the MioFuse I was offered to review.
I just don't understand the lack of a functional timer but other than that, especially if you're a runner, I'd say it's worth it.

review_text:
I dreaded joining the masses and getting one of them new fangled smart watches that counts your steps, reads your text messages, makes your coffee in the morning, etc. I feared becoming dependent on it like our current generation has become with their smart phones. Nose in the screen, only to look up when a slice of pizza is thrust between them and the screen. I considered myself a classic watch collector and wearer. The ol' tick tock watches. Remember those? But alas, I needed a new running watch (my forerunner 10 bit the dust), so I figured I may as well upgrade considering these Garmins are dirt cheap now (my first garmin gps watch was over 200 dollars back in 2003 and all it did was tell time and pace). Holy sh*t, this Forerunner 35 is amazing, and I will admit I rarely take it off, against my previous stubborn attitude. I've even developed a watch tan. Ive never had a watch tan in my life and I'm the watch guy in my friend group, and I spend countless hours a week outside running and at the lake fishing. The text feature is convenient, the heart rate and step count features and helpful, and it even tracks how long you sleep! Features aside, it is well made, sleek, stylish, and the battery life lasts surprisingly long (I rarely drop below 1 bar and only need to charge it a couple of hours for an entire week's use. I can't find anything to hate about this watch (maybe a split screen feature like my past garmins that shows curent pace, avg pace, distance, etc. on one screen). But I can live without that for 120 dollars. I hope this watch has a long life because I love it.

*Update*: Still love the watch, but I looked down today during a long bike ride and the watch screen had separated from the body. Seems as if the glue melted? I tried popping it back in as I rode but the smallest bump would cause it to pop back out. It still works. I ran some E6000 glue around the edges when I got home. Hopefully it holds. I also *thought* I heard something drop on the ground just before i looked down and noticed the watch had separated, so I'm hoping a vital part did not fall out. Dropping to 4 starts for less than ideal craftsmanship. Will update again if something indeed is wrong with it.

My old Charge HR (7 years old now?) would constantly read my heartrate, where this reads every 10 minutes by default with a shortest read time of 1 minute, so I'm not sure how it could possibly get accurate reads during workout periods since heartrates go up and down quickly between sprints.

Do not recommend anyone purchase this.

The watch materials are underwhelming and it just feels so…cheap..it’s actually mind blowing.. I’d pay $30 happily and $40 max with a 2nd amendment item pointed to my head. (If the step counter was fixed)
The app is great however. I DON’T recommend this watch and am disappointed as the Amazfit Band 3 turned me on to wearables initially, it seems that the smartwatch mid-range is not a place to be taking risks with lesser known names in the game.
If you need something for heart rate and something to track your steps just get something cheap like an older fitbit for mid range and budget range or an Amazfit band under $30..don’t fall for the added gimmick of extra features at premium price that you’ll more than likely never utilize.

At the end of the day this will “get you by and do the job” if you get it as a gift, find one on the side of the road or find it on clearance. However I expected better MUCH better for the money spent.

review_text:
For some reason, it seems that the $100 price point is the dividing line for Amazfit products being decent/working well, and not. To explain..... I have purchased 3 Amazfit watches, starting with this one. There are issues and disappointments with all of them, however, this particular watch worked OK for about 4 days/nights, then it would randomly reset itself, and in the process delete all data it had accumulated. That was what made me return it.
A couple of very annoying things with this particular watch....
1. SP02 has no automatic feature/setting. Meaning that the only way it will take a reading is if you do it manually.
2. The zepp app that is required with these watches is annoying because each watch displays a bit differently on the app, due to various watches having given functions or not. But the real annoyance is syncing data, which seems to have a mind of its own.... if I try to make it sync sometimes it will, and other times not.
3. DO NOT believe the claims on battery life! With the features I wanted turned on, the best I could get was 2 days/nights on a charge!
4. Finally, ALL of the Amazfit products I've purchased have absolutely horrible documentation! The included manual is very ambiguous, and you can't figure out how anything works using it. I had to search the web and comb through far too many YouTube videos to find the information needed. The amount of time and effort wasted searching for "how to" information is enough cause a 1 star rating!

Many online reviews rate this watch as "Best Cheap Smart Watch"...... but I'd highly recommend either going with another brand at this price point, or higher price points in this brand. Go with their GTR or S or higher. I think their GTR/S 2e is the best bang for the buck, although it has the same faults and horrible documentation as the rest.

review_title: Great fitness watch, has the features I desired at a reasonable price.
review_text:
I've been using it for over a month now and I love it. I'm an older person who really just wanted to track my steps and my sleep. But I didn't want something that had to be charged very often or cost a lot of money like an Apple watch or the Fitbit bands. This fits the bill. I can track my steps on the watch, or in the app. I can even set the watch up so that it lets me know when I have hit my goal...nice!. I can also set a timer to get me moving if I sit too long. These need to be set up in the app. I can set an alarm TIME in the app, and then switch it on or off directly on the watch. There are many other things this watch can do, but those are the main ones I use. I just checked the app, The watch says 23 days since last charge and I'm on 42% battery life. Love that!

Keep in mind that supposedly the GPS function uses a lot of battery life. Most people shut it off when not using it. You can find out more about that function and lots of others by checking out the many, many YouTube videos about this watch. It is very popular, and that's a good thing. If you have a question or a problem, there's probably others that had the same problem, that means there's probably a video or at the very least a web page somewhere that can help you!

The Mi Fit app will keep stats for the activities and keep history so you can see how consistent you are in your activities. It has a small section for the sleep tracking, however I would advise anyone who really wants to track their sleep to get the free Android app "Notify & Fitness for Amazfit". You can find it in the Google Play store by the GREEN icon. It interprets the sleep functions even better, and I KNOW the sleep times are more accurate than the Mi Fit app. The "Notify" app will also track the other fitness functions similar to Me Fit, but they each have their pros and cons. I choose to use them both, but that would be a personal decision.

Supposedly you can use "Notify" without the Mi Fit app even being installed on the phone, however the Mi Fit app has the built-in way to change the watch face, so I really don't want to uninstall it. Which leads me to one of my favorite things about this watch: the user created faces. There are faces for every age and need and in quite a few languages! I wanted something with good utility, but there are fun ones with Simpsons and comic characters, etc. Those are too busy or make it hard to find the info I need. The stock faces are all pretty usable, but the main reason that I wanted to change from the stock ones is that I wanted 12 hour time display. FYI, most of the faces that come with the Mi Fit app show 24 hour time instead of 12 hour AM/PM time. Some people, like military may prefer the 24 hour display...but I'm so glad that they gave the ability to change.

To get 12 hour time, I had to find a way to install third party faces. (Mini tutorial is below) There are several apps on the Play Store that make changing the watch face easy, the one I prefer is "My Watchface [Free] for Amazfit Bip" It has quite a few faces, and allows you to switch out the ones that are in the Mi Fit app so that you can use your replacements directly from the Mi Fit app. It includes a screen that shows you which of the original faces you have switched out so you can easily go back and forth. Some people save the faces on their computer and do it the hard way. This way is much easier! Trust me!

I haven't even set up the phone notification functions, because my phone is always in my pocket anyway. I can see where those might be useful for some people but not me.

I'm in Florida so this time of year it's not good to get out and walk and for very long. I plan on setting up the GPS functions this fall when the temperature drops a bit. But really I can see from other reviews that it should work fine.

All around good watch. I'm very happy with my purchase.

My Pics in order:

Showing the visibility of the watch face:

Watch face-darkest ambient light (The camera lightened the pic a bit. It was really too dark to read it.)
Watch face-dark ambient light-somewhat readable
Watch face-lit ONLY by overhead light-very readable (No backlight)
Watch face-lit by overhead light with backlight on
Watch face-lit in dark room with backlight on

Screenshots of the two fitness apps:

Mi Fit app home screen (tap on each section to drill down)
Mi Fit Sleep app (only showing a portion of the info available)
Notify & Fitness app home screen (tap on each section to drill down)

Watchfaces:

My Watchface [Free] for Amazfit Bip app, showing the replaced watch faces side by side with the original faces...original on left, replacement faces on right (app w black background)

Watch faces (originals) from the Mi Fit app.(App w white background)

These last two pics are provided to illustrate my mini tutorial on how to change from the stock watch face:

Using "My Watchface [Free] for Amazfit Bip": After you have picked a replacement face in the watchface app, you decide which of the faces in the Mi Fit app you want to over-write. In this case, I am over-writing the Temple face. Once you have done this (using the watchface app), go to the Mi Fit app and click on the Temple face, and your replacement (in this example, the one showing a time of 5:40), will be the one that is transferred to your watch. And you can see that the one in the side by side pics shows the face in all my pics is the one beside the Temple pic...voila!

This Watchface app will let you overwrite a few of the Mi Fit watch faces, and you can overwrite even more of them if you buy the app.

I knew I was never going to use the Temple face so I had no concern about not having access to it. There probably is a way to get that original face back, but I really am not sure, and I really don't care because all of these are 24 hour faces that I would never use anyway!

Hope this helps someone!

Paying attention, Garmin? Vivosmart only has one alarm, so, for example, I couldn't configure one alarm for weekdays and a separate on for weekends. The Amazfit Bip sets a new standard for fitness trackers and smartwatches as far as I am concerned.

review_title: As CNET says: Best cheap alternative to Apple Watch
review_text: I've had this watch for about two weeks now and I'm completely happy with it.  As you can see in the photo, I chose a watchface that gives me what I need:  Time, day/date; weather forecast; battery life.  Down below you'll see the tracker info:  Calories, steps and heart rate.  Yes, my battery life is at 32% after two weeks.  Awesome, huh?  I do have the heartbeat monitor set to every 10 minutes also and wear the watch at night to use the Sleep Tracker.  ADVICE:  There are no instructions with this watch.  You have to go to their website to get started. The app for this watch is MiFit.  The MiFit app is where you can see all your info, settings, activity, sleep tracker, etc.  The activity app is very cool.  I run, so it shows me the map of the run, time, pace (time/graph, by mile), calories, heart rate/zone, elevation.  Easy to use.  Settings app is for what displays on the watch.  I, of course, get phone calls, texts, and some app notifications (if I have them on).  Be careful if you get alot of app notifications as your watch will be vibrating constantly. I turned off the Messenger notifications because it was too much.  There is an Amazfit Tools app that gives you more options, syncs with the iPhone Health app and also has more watch faces available (those watch faces are also international, so the time, day, etc can be in a foreign language.  I didn't care for many of them).  Watch is nice, light, sleek.  The only gripes I have is it sometimes is slow to update the current temperature (also, if you have trouble with the auto-detect setting for weather, try choosing a location.  If find this works much better, but it won't change when you go somewhere else).  And I can't say the sleep tracker is entirely accurate.  It's pretty close on the amount of time, but the deep sleep/light sleep portions are a mystery to me.  One feature I do like is an activity monitor so it will buzz me every hour if it detects I haven't been moving (probably through the step tracker) and I like that so I get out of my chair at work.  All in all, I think this watch is great, the battery life is phenomenal and if you don't need all that fancy Apple Watch stuff, it's a win.

review_title: Not for use as a HR monitor. Update 4/17.
review_text:
Initially the HR monitor seemed to work quite well and correlate to a chest strap. However as updates have occurred the device has gotten much worse to the point of being ineffective for measurement of HR. If you rely on HR in your workout routines DO NOT buy this device, use a chest strap. Today I did my usual row where my HR settles at 160 for the major of the rowing session. With this device it measured anywhere from 65 to 90 for the duration. This has been going on for a few weeks now and even with cycling power it is totally inaccurate.

I can only assume Garmin did updates that rendered this device useless for HR measurements. Not worth the price of entry.

I do like the other features such as GPS tracking for my outdoor activities, timer, elevation, etc. However this is quite expensive without effective HR data.

UPDATE 4/17. Device will not sync to Garmin connect via USB cable. And the screen is now burned in with the clock. Did not use for about a week and the clock is now embedded in screen. So when you switch to another view the clock is visible while you are trying to read the settings, or select a workout routine. Product is 8 months old. We shall see how effective the warranty is now.

review_text:
I really wanted to like this watch. I've had Garmin running watches in the past and while they are occasionally glitchy, they do a good job of tracking distance and pace. Having a functional smartwatch with the strong activity/GPS tracking of traditional Garmin products would be a real step forward.

Unfortunately, this is not that watch. It worked okay for a few days, but then started rebooting itself multiple times a day, including during runs - when this happens, you not only lose functionality (including the watch face) but often lose any data since last reboot. The connection with phone app (Garmin Connect mobile) is sketchy as best - sometimes it works, a lot of times it can't make connection and sync. Right now, the watch function is insisting that it is Saturday instead of Monday, and there's no way to fix, apparently.

It's a shame because in a lot of ways this is a really useful product. It's small and light enough to wear as an everyday watch, and the GPS (when it works) is good for tracking pace and distance. It also provides weather and text alerts when the phone sync is working, which is nice to have, especially if you aren't carrying a phone.

I've seen other reviews that suggest that this is not everyone's experience, so wouldn't base the decision to purchase on this review alone - just be aware that it may have software issues.

Terrible. I have owned this watch for about 4 months. If I could go back in time and buy another activity tracker instead of this one, I would. I primarily wanted a watch that would let me track daily steps, HR, and running. I really wanted to love this watch and at first it seemed great. Then I started noticing numerous activity tracking inaccuracies and started dealing with the many glitches and freeze ups this watch has. I went in to this realizing that wrist trackers are normally +/- 10% inaccurate. I can accept that, but I believe this tracker to frequently be >20% inaccurate. My overall disappointment with this device is such that I don't think I will ever buy another Garmin product again. I personally find the numerous very positive reviews very suspect.

Pros - Long battery life. I can easily get by for a week on one charge, however I do not use the GPS feature very frequently so I can't speak to the battery life for that. Screen is bright enough to read even outside on a sunny day.

Note - The watch is somewhat large. I sometimes have a hard time fitting it under a dress shirt cuff. The plastic is somewhat cheap looking, but has held up well. No scratches so far.

Cons - Too many to name them all, but here are some of the most frustrating. The watch is inaccurate in every activity that it tracks to the extent that the data collected is nearly useless. Step tracking is off frequently by >20%. The watch will frequently freeze up and stop counting steps. When I start tracking a run, about 10% of the time the watch will freeze up. When it restarts it will have lost all data for the day (good bye 10K step day). Sleep tracking is often off by hours, there is no way to manually set the tracker in sleep mode as many other devices can be. When I have used GPS to track an outdoor walks the line it draws on the map squiggles around so much that it adds a significant amount of "phantom" distance to the activity. I took a walk that was .75 miles as measured on google maps, the watch indicated 1.1 miles (46% bonus distance?). The watch has randomly changed time on me twice and was off by more than 2 hours. Can I count on my morning alarm to go off at the right time? I bought the Garmin chest strap and foot pod to sync with the watch, but have been less than pleased. Both frequently disconnect from the watch during activity causing data loss or inaccuracy. The vibration mode is heard more than felt. It vibrates too loudly for a quiet setting.

Extra Bad Con - Heart rate tracking seems to be a whole extra level of inaccuracy. In the morning I have a resting heart rate of around 58-62 most days. The watch will accurately reflect this reading all day long, however over night it will change the resting heart rate for the previous day by 10-20 bpm. When viewing the 'all day heart rate' in the app, it will reflect readings that do not match the data on the watch at all. There is this weird disconnect between the watch and the Garmin software. On a day that I had no strenuous activity the watch indicated a max heart rate of 110 for the day. When I viewed the data on the Garmin app it had instead logged a max heart rate of 150. How does the data that is collected and stored on the watch not match the data on the app/website? Are we just making up numbers here?

2) Sleep tracking - a joke again. The moment you settle in bed the watch thinks you are sleeping - if it's late enough. The difference between actual sleep and recorded sleep can be easily 2-3 hours. Daytime naps are not recorded. This is not sleep tracking by any measure. And I know it can be done better. Again, Charge HR was tracking my sleep beautifully.
3) No way to add other sports (ex. tennis). How hard is to let the user define a name for an activity that is tracked like a predefined one (indoor running for ex.).

In essence great hardware, but very disappointing implementation of certain features I like. In fact I would call it misleading advertisement!!!

--Brief notes on the pros and cons of the Vivoactive HR--

Pros
* having a wrist-based GPS is great for running and biking and eliminates any need to carry a phone
* using tracking for running and biking is easy, and the device switches easily from watch to sport mode
* doesn't look out of place or too bulky on the wrist
* Garmin Connect app seems to work reasonably well

Cons
* device is not appropriate for wear during all exercise: the glass cracked within a month of buying it, rendering the touch screen unusable (more on this below)
* useless for tracking general exercise (I do CrossFit), other than the general measure of heart-rate, which isn't terribly accurate
* while the watch is not terribly bulky, wearing it 24/7 is not practical. It's uncomfortable to sleep with.
* the on-screen messages from my phone are 90% useless. While it's somewhat useful to be able to see who is calling on one's wrist, having truncated versions of every phone notification on the wrist is superfluous.

About the cracked glass: Garmin is charging me $99 to send a replacement watch, but I am assuming that if I continue to wear the device while working out that it will almost certainly crack again. I have no idea how it broke the first time, but assume that my wrist must have banged something during a CrossFit workout. Cracked glass is considered an out-of-warranty repair.

review_title: I am very disappointed with this watch!
review_text:
I bought this watch for my wife for Christmas. It is now the end of February and it has completely stopped functioning. It claims to be water resistant to 50 meters, however, she was wearing hers in the shower and that seems to be what ruined it. At first the screen went black when she got out of the shower. After letting it dry for a couple of weeks, the display started working again (but only as a display - the touchscreen is still not working anymore).

I am very disappointed with Garmin. Other products we own from them have been much more solid. This is a very poorly designed watch.

I take negative reviews (and all reviews for that matter) very seriously because I depend on them to make my decisions. I tend to weed out those reviews that are too emotionally charged (either for or against) and look for honest assessments of the product. This watch is not worth buying - look around and find something else, you'll be glad if you did.

In addition to the obvious fact that our watch no longer works, it was flawed from the onset. The interface is not very intuitive at all. A lot of devices now a days are user friendly, this one is not. The user must dig through poorly designed sub menus to access common features. It's Bluetooth connectivity is also very poorly designed. It doesn't connect via the standards that we all know and understand, instead it requires creating a connection through an app on the phone. This app is also incredibly poorly designed. It is hard to figure out where things are, and things that one might expect to be on the first window to open are buried several pages away. A good example of this is the ability to sync the two devices together. Since this is the very first thing needed to be done ever time the program is launched (and arguably the most important) I would expect a large and obvious "sync button" to be one of the first things that catches my eye when I launch the app. It is not. The ability to sync is buried deep into the app (several pages away) in a place that is not very obvious at all. Digging through their app is similar to a game of concentration, knowing that you found it once before seems to be the only motivation for continuing on with the hunt.

Obviously with a watch costing as much as this one does, with flawed software and ceasing to work after sixty day my experience is negative. I am not being emotionally charged in my assessment, rather telling you about this experience so that you might make an informed decision as to whether or not you are willing to take the risk.

review_title: So what did I find good about the Vivioactive watch
review_text:
I am a keen cyclist, swimmer and golfer who originally studied Sports Science, so I was excited about the all around potential of the watch.
So what did I find good about the Vivioactive watch?
It did calculate a resting heart rate for each day, which is useful for judging recovery.
The battery life was reasonable, I got 5-7 days.
The GPS and motion for the activity tracker worked well to track steps and km.

What did I find bad about it?
The screen is fragile, not suitable for sporting use, worse than the old iphones.
The apps are substantially inferior to the dedicated sporting equivalent, the cycling one has less than my old Garmin edge 500. The golf one I see little benefit in using. The sleep app doesn't work, the data is meaningless and wrong.
The software is clunky and accessing menus is worse than a Nokia phone from a decade ago.
The Heart rate monitor should be called non-elevate, as it does not work with any reliability for exercise. I did the Cradle Mountain peaks challenge bike ride, 10 hours of hard riding. According to the watch, I had zero intensity minutes for that week. It is OK for resting heart rates, but for exercise I found it worse than other reviewers, it didn't lag, it just didn't function, I would go so far as to say for effective exercise heart rate monitoring you have to use a chest strap with it.

In summary, a product that I was disappointed with before it broke. Based on my experience, I would say it is not for outdoor use (my screen broke inside with a casual bang against a piece of furniture). Garmin declined to help, other than offering a refurbished replacement unit at 45% of new price. It broke inside 2 months of use. I would not buy again, based on support experience I will not buy any Garmin product ever again. Garmin Australia are not prepared to stand behind their product. Other users have reported on other forums the same problem of the screens breaking in normal use.

review_text:
Update:

I have now also tested this against the Fitbit Versa 4, and the Garmin wins by a landslide. While the Versa does have much better sleep tracking and I like that you can count distance instead of steps, the UI is terrible and the touch-screen isn’t very responsive. Also, only a very short list of iPhone apps integrate, so I couldn’t get WhatsApp and a few other frequently used apps’ notifications to the Versa. On top of all that, it was unnecessarily bulky.

My main beef with Garmin remains the sleep tracking. I also wish you could track distance vs steps and that you could still see the time of day when you’re tracking a workout. I still absolutely love the UI surrounding the timers. I use them multipe times a day while cooking or doing chores, and it’s so simple to just swipe and type in a number. I also love how you can make the timer repeat so easily if you’re doing intervals (although I do wish you could set alternating intervals). It’s truly amazing how something so simple can affect your life. I don’t think I’ll ever switch to another watch.

Original review:

I’ve had four fitness trackers in my life: a Fitbit Flex 2, an Apple Watch, and a Fitbit Charge 4. My main needs are step counting, sleep tracking, timers, and phone alerts. Here is what I’ll say about the Vivoactive 4s.

Step counting is pretty accurate, but I don’t know of any watches that do this poorly. I do wish that you could add steps manually. I have a treadmill desk, and the watch won’t count those steps or track the treadmill workout - I think the watch can’t register my motions because my wrists aren’t moving. Not a big deal because my treadmill counts steps, but I wish I could merge them with my Garmin data. That’s my only beef with the app interface and movement tracking.

The GPS works great, and it’s fun to see your little map on the watch face itself. My husband also has a Garmin, but it doesn’t have that feature. One weird thing about the GPS is that there is a screen within the GPS interface that has a whole mess of little icons. I assume those are meant to be plotted on a map, but I can’t figure out how or where to do this. The manual doesn’t address it.

I will say the sleep tracking leaves something to be desired, and the quality is poor enough to knock a full star off the overall rating. It’s a huge step down from Fitbit, which is by far the best at sleep tracking - it will even track naps. The Vivoactive’s tracking is wildly inaccurate. It rarely records my sleep times correctly and sometimes thinks I’m asleep when I’m just watching tv or reading at night. This is the only way in which the watch lets me down, and it is a significant disappointment. It’s not as bad as the Apple watch, though. At least you don’t have to remember to turn on a completely separate app when you go to sleep.

The O2 sensor isn’t important to me, but it does drain your battery in a big way. I don’t think it’s very accurate, either, so I turned it off.

I do like the interface. It’s way more customizable than the Fitbit and Apple watches, and you can rearrange your menus and also hide things you don’t care about. You can also turn off the light entirely. I have my right-swipe shortcut set to the facelight dimmer, so I turn it all the way down at bedtime. I really like the Find My Phone button, although if you press it accidentally while you’re holding your phone, you get a bit of a jolt!

I think you can do voice calling with this watch, but I don’t have an Android. The call/text/other notifications work fine with my iPhone.

One of my main beefs with the Charge 4 was that it vibrated. Like constantly vibrated anytime you scrolled through a menu or touched it at all, and you couldn’t turn it off entirely. The Vivoactive has customizable vibration intensity, and it only vibrates for notifications and confirmations.

The timer on this watch is by far my favorite. I cook often, and having a timer on my wrist is super convenient. I love that you type in the time instead of scrolling. Such a simple feature, but it’s completely painless.

All in all, I would 100% recommend this watch. If you don’t take into account sleep tracking, I give it five stars.

review_text:
I bought the vivoactive 4S to replace my Fitbit Versa 2 that had to be replaced twice because of hardware issues. I also wanted to switch because I felt garmin provided more stars and what not that mattered to me. Onboard GPS, Spotify music storage, ability to connect to a chest heart rate monitor for more accurate HR readings, and the body battery are just a few of the things that sold me on it!

I don’t regret my purchase at all, but a few things in the future I wish garmin would work on:
1.) Speedier bug fixes for iOS
2.) Sleep tracking algorithm/sensitivity
3.) Third-party band compatibility

———-
1.) The day I purchased this watch, iOS 13.4 was released and it created an issue where I cannot clear my notifications. After contacting garmin support, I was told it will be fixed in the coming weeks.

2.) The sleep tracking is not super accurate so far

3.) Third party bands do work sometimes, but the 18mm lug is actually bigger than most standard 18mm lugs due to manufacturing inconsistencies.

Overall, 4/5!

review_text:
I’ve used Garmin fitness watches for the past 10 years, starting with the very basic Forerunner 25. The Vivoactive 4 is my 6th Garmin watch (all the previous watches were still functioning fine when I retired them). My use has gone from run tracking to more health/fitness tracking. My training consist of kettlebells and a spin bike (with a Garmin cadence sensor). I also use a Garmin HRM Dual chest strap as I feel it is more accurate then the optical sensors on fitness watches, especially when exercising.

I have had this watch for a month. The Vivoactive 4 is, quite simply, the best Garmin I have owned. It captures health data (stress, Body Battery, sleep) quite easily. Capturing training data is also done well. I particularly like the display. It is large which is a plus for my aging eyes. It is always on but not lit up as with some watches. A flip of the wrist will activate the light to make the display quite readable in the dark. I actually disabled this feature except while training which conserves battery life. I leave the feature on during training as my training corner is not terribly well lit.

It syncs seamlessly with Garmin Connect on my iPhone. I have no problem with the widgets or data fields functioning properly.

I’m still exploring more of the functions and possibilities for this watch and how it can impact my health and fitness.

For those who are looking for an affordable, easy to operate fitness watch that will give you what probably 95% of the population can use, this is your watch.

review_title: Dreadful as a heart rate monitor, and customer service is not helpful
review_text:
In summary: once you touch the heart icon, you will probably have to endure an interminable wait for a reading to be displayed; and, that reading is likely to be wrong; and, in any event, the display will likely time out after a few seconds and lose the reading.

I bought this thing primarily for use as a heartbeat rate monitor. If following your HBR is your primary interest, this fitness tracker (Fitpolo ID205L) will be essentially useless. (For other uses, I am not qualified to comment.)

“Essentially” useless, not completely, because it sometimes does get it right. Those occasions do indeed occur; but, like leap years or the passage of popular comets, those occurrences will not be frequent. Sometimes, perhaps one time in twenty, the monitor will display the heartbeat rate immediately after the heart icon is touched. Sometimes, perhaps one in twenty, the HBR will display for a substantial number of seconds before the display times out and the reading is lost. More typically, after the heart icon is touched, the display reads “—bpm,” and it typically reports –bpm for 18 to 30 seconds. After the passage of the requisite number of seconds, it will often display a heartbeat rate…some heartbeat rate, not necessarily yours…and, after a few seconds, it will time out and lose the reading. At that point, one must start over.

On many occasions, the watch will display “—bpm” interminably, and then time out, having never provided a reading.

As for the accuracy of the readings: The readings seem to be more-or-less correct, at lower levels of exertion. At high levels, the readings are wrong. I have been training with heart rate monitors for 28 years. I know when my heart is running at over 130 bpm, but the Fitpolo smartwatch will report something between 100 and 107.

A few minutes ago, it gave me a reading of 147 bpm. I was sitting here, typing. So, even at lower levels of exertion, the readings are not necessarily reliable.

This is listed as “Amazon’s Choice in Smartwatches by Fitpolo.” I leave it to you to decide whether this speaks more to the quality of Amazon’s choices or to that of Fitpolo’s smartwatches.

I must also mention that someone from Fitpolo’s customer service did contact me…unsolicited…and offered to be helpful. I wrote to this person, “Barbara.” Barbara was not helpful. I will return the watch to Amazon.

The app, VeryFitPro, rates only 3.1 stars in Google Play Station. Based on my experience with the app, I consider that rating to be extremely over-generous.

I hope this helps.

The compass on the Galaxy watch app requires you to do a crappy figure 8 motion to calibrate it, and it works just as horribly as it does on android phones (that is a big reason why I need a watch, because android often shows inaccurate facing direction in google maps, for 10+ years it has not been fixed- IOS doesn't have this issue at all).
6) A bunch of super annoying stuff is enabled as a default. Your watch will be vibrating all the time just to tell you that you are walking somewhere. The thing is I want the sleep function but I don't want all of the auto tracking and other annoying notifications (which no doubt make the battery life so bad). Shealth doesn't seem to have the ability to tweak enough to make this possible. If I walk 10 minutes to the train station, I get a notification that I'm walking. So I start ignoring my notifications. review_title: Most of the features do not work
review_text:
I bought this watch primarily to keep track of my heart rate without having to use my pulse oximeter. The watch consistently shows that my heart rate is ten beats higher than what my pulse oximeter says. My pulse oximeter works and is accurate and I've compared it to readings at my doctor's office and the hospital. I set up vibrating alerts for low and high heart rate. My heart can go to under 50bpm and as high as 160bpm. I set the alert for under 60bpm and higher than 110bpm. My heart has definitely reached the low end and high end of the spectrum and I haven't received any alerts.

The oxygen saturation detection does not work. It is consistently 10-20 percentage points below what my pulse oximeter says.

The fall detection does not work whatsoever. I have fallen several times while wearing my watch even after I toggled the option to be more sensitive to falls. It did alert me of a "fall" when I was slapping my leg to get my dog to come to me, but when I've fallen really hard, the fall alert has not come up.

I am a small person, meaning my wrists are also small. They measure 5.25" around. The small watch band is too big even on the smallest setting. Also, because of the way the band folds under the watch, it makes the watch not sit completely flat. One side is slightly raised. I can easily fit two fingers under the band.

The sleep tracker is not accurate. It has said I'm awake when I am most definitely asleep and vice versa.

The pedometer feature does not work. It counts steps when I'm literally doing yoga on the ground.

Overall, this watch was a complete waste of money. I would advise anyone to get an iPhone and then get an Apple watch. Samsung missed the mark entirely.

review_text:
This is the second Samsung Gear watch that I've bought and hated. I love Fitbits, but I'm sick of spending the money just for them to stop working within 12-18 months, so I went back to Samsung. All I really wanted was a fitness tracker, which this can do. I don't need all the extra stuff, I have a phone for everything else. I'm 100% Team Samsung, but these watches are awful. Even with every single thing but the actual clock turned off, I get maybe a day and a half of battery life. I turn on the Bluetooth for maybe 2-3 minutes a day to sync my data. That's it. If you charge it before bed and put it on, you lose 15% of the battery just sleeping WITH NO GPS, BLUETOOTH, ALWAYS ON DISPLAY, OR WIFI ON. That's unacceptable.
The Samsung Health app is garbage, too. It's not as intuitive or fluent as Fitbit and doesn't sync quickly at all. The steps are way off, too. I walked in the treadmill for an hour twice last week and it only caught 37 minutes the first time and 28 the second time, while only logging about 3500 steps each time, which isn't even close to 4 miles worth of steps.
It's a nice looking watch and has a lot of features if you don't mind charging it daily, which means you'll miss out on things while it's always charging.
All in all I'm stuck with another $250 paper weight and am in the search for another fitness tracker.

review_title: As of 10/26/2021, unacceptably poor battery life and overheading problems
review_text:
First, I want to make it clear that I am VERY familiar with Samsung smart watches and their configuration, I have owned several previous models and have spent a considerably amount of time delving into their setup menus to configure them for optimal use.

So I was astounded when I upgraded to a 44mm LTE Watch 4 and was unable to get more than 8 hours on a charge even with LTE, wifi, and bluetooth disabled, and after all software updates as of 10/26/21 had been applied.

At first I assumed that either I was dealing with a defective watch or that the watch was misconfigured, but a web search revealed that many users were having a similar or even worse experience, and that though Samsung is aware of the problem and has released a set of recommenced configuration choices to improve battery life specifically to address the Watch 4 issues, for many users battery life still remains abysmal.

In addition, many users report having an additional problem I'm experiencing: when making a cellular call, the watch overheats and disconnects 2-5 minutes into every call, you are is locked out of using the phone while it cools, and that this happens even at locations with a strong cellular signal - in addition to accounts posted in various discussion groups, there are several recent YouTube videos documenting this problem.

I realize that there are many reviews here by users who are getting somewhat better battery life, and that it's temping to assume that reports of poor battery life are the result of misconfiguration or simply expecting too much of the watch in terms of enabled functionality vs run time on a charge.

However, go to Samsung's own site (Amazon no longer allows embed external links in reviews, so you will have to do a web search yourself) and then search tor "battery life:", you will find MANY example of frustrated Watch 4 and Watch 4 Classic owners who have done everything recommended by Samsung tech support and still can't get more than 6-12 hours on a charge, even on non LTE watches and with Bluetooth and wifi disabled.

And if you are one of them, as I was before returning this watch, a Watch 4 is going to require at least one additional two hour recharge to get through an 16 hour day.

review_title: Amazing fitness tracker but not yet smartwatch
review_text:
Battery life: Fitbit claims the Sense can last up to six days (6 days+) on a single charge when it used smartwatch mode (i.e. no GPS usage). However, that battery life on Fitibit sense is not much accurate the watch only lasting of 4 out 5 days of battery life short of what Fitbit promises.

Sleep tracking: The Fitbit Sense smartwatch on sleep tracking, is accurate and on point to showing data of how much you sleep during night giving a sleeping score. Only downside, its that much of the necessary data of sleep is attached to premium account which requires monthly $9.99 payment. An important update that was made on Fitibit Sense smartwatch, its the addition of stress management and how to treat stress on day to day basis.

Mobile App: Fitbit sense smartwatch when it comes to application, still on primitive state not much has improved at all much of third party application but not major application from big player like Google Maps; Lyft; uber eats or grubhub or Domino's. Its major let down to see major app missing which will make the watch more interesting. Its sad that Fitibit has been releasing versa for awhile now and it doesn’t look like the app ecosystem is making much progress since 2017 - which is a bit disappointing.

End of review: the Fitbit Sense despite its app selection shortcomings, the sense does offer to be an impressive fitness tracker with sleep tracking perfection. It nailed the basics, and this new generation of Fitbit has improved so much to include the ability to take phone calls on the watch; ECG which is super sweet buy for yourself or family members. But on the smartwatch side of things, is a little limited and it's not much of smartwatch compare to other devices on the market. But definitely is buy if you only care for fitness.

review_text:
I've had the Sense for 3 months now, prior to that I had a Charge 4.
This smartwatch suites my needs. I did a lot of research online between the Sense and some of the Garmin products and a Fitbit flash sale was the deciding factor.
I have to say that I agree with many other reviews about the heart rate being off at times, it does not agree with the hand held heart rate monitor while using the elliptical, the Sense is lower. After spending 10 minutes or more on the elliptical, the Sense catches up. That's a disappointment for sure and my biggest gripe.

I do a fair amount of cycling and although I don't start the watch in "bike" mode, it knows I'm on an "outdoor bike ride" and measures my heart rate throughout the ride and counts some of my pedaling as steps and gives a summary of calories burned. It just doesn't have a GPS summary at the end of the ride ( I have a Garmin cycle computer for that). If I start the ride in "bike mode" it will show a map of where I've been, it's pretty consistent to my Garmin, including elevation climbed.

The battery life is not 6 days, I charge mine every 3-4 days, not sure how they come up with that claim.
There's dozens of clock faces to choose from in the Fitbit app and the app will warn you if it's not Fitbit approved. I don't know what harm will be done but I'm happy with the basic ones.
The settings let you customize many features, for example, I don't want to be notified that it's time to move. I found that annoying.
So, do your research online or YouTube, there's many videos to watch and of course, it's someone else's opinion when you're watching on YouTube.
